# Forty-Eight Hours in Porto

I arrived in Porto on a Friday afternoon with a loose plan and a pair of comfortable shoes, and by Sunday evening I was already planning my return. The city shows itself slowly, one tiled facade and crooked cobblestone lane at a time.

Saturday began at Livraria Lello, a bookshop with carved wooden shelves and a scarlet staircase. Go early, buy your ticket ahead, and leave time to look up at the stained-glass ceiling.

For lunch I had a francesinha at Café Santiago: a tall sandwich of cured meats and steak, covered in melted cheese and soaked in a tomato-beer sauce. At 6 euros, it was the best-value meal of the trip, and I regret nothing.

The Dom Luís I Bridge at sunset was the last stop. The Douro turned gold, and the whole city seemed to exhale.
